correctness.rationale: A complete 24-root and 276-pair enumeration proves the exact distance thresholds. All 96 radius-one triangles coincide with octahedral facet triangles, so K1 is the 2-skeleton of a convex 4-polytope boundary; removing 24 open facet balls proves a wedge of 23 spheres. At radius two, 12 antipodal forbidden pairs give a 12-fold S0 join homeomorphic to S11. The oriented cellular boundary gives the precise free integral signed facet quotient. All four F4 generating reflections have determinant -1 and orientation degree -1 on the cross-polytope sphere; they generate all 1152 graph automorphisms. The checker independently enumerates graph automorphisms, fixed-facet traces and triangle-boundary mod-two rank, corroborating the exact integral proof. Risks: the finite checker supplements but does not replace the manifold and group-orientation arguments.

value.rationale: The 24-cell is the exceptional regular 4-polytope with full W(F4) symmetry. Numerical homology of its geometric Rips filtration was previously recorded, but the full integral W(F4) persistence modules distinguish a geometric orientation twist and quotient facet-permutation lattice, compute an exact seven-value character on all 1152 elements and show absence of invariant positive-degree classes. These are natural equivariant invariants not recoverable from Betti numbers, useful for comparisons of symmetric 4-polytope metrics. The object and invariant are canonical rather than an arbitrary slice. Limits: only one polytope and no classification of arbitrary root graphs.
